overall: The AG found the Amherst Board of Registrars did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the April 21 notice was sufficiently specific, no improper email, serial, phone or in-person deliberation was shown, and the Charter delegation claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 21 notice topic, delegating Charter Sections 8.2-8.4 duties to Town Clerk staff, was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Because the April 21 meeting notice described the anticipated topic with sufficient specificity—namely, the delegation of certain duties and authorities to Town Clerk's Office staff—and that is in fact what the Board discussed during the April 21 meeting, we find that the notice for the April 21 meeting was sufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly delegated its authority to the Town Clerk in violation of the Amherst Town Charter.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of  the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. Accordingly, we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated by email outside a posted meeting before its April 21 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that any emails that did not reach a quorum, or were merely about scheduling or agenda items and did not express opinions of public body members, did not constitute deliberation for purposes of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A May 13 email by one member forwarding public-records responses to a quorum was reviewed as possible improper deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this purely administrative task did not constitute improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged serial communication, or phone or in-person deliberation, by a quorum ahead of the April 21 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find no evidence that the Board communicated in a serial manner or deliberated either by phone or in-person ahead of the April 21 meeting.
